traits.inflorescence.note: DELTA Amaranthaceae (read 2026-10-17): flowers in cymes, spikes or heads; Wikipedia (read 2026-10-17) adds panicles. Weighting by genus size: the chenopod genera (Atriplex ~300, Salsola s.l., Suaeda, Chenopodium s.l., Salicornia), over half the ~2,000+ spp, bear glomerules in spikes or spiciform panicles, as do Achyranthes and Amaranthus; heads mainly in Gomphrena and Alternanthera (~250-300). Genus sizes are approximate, not from the pages.

traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA, Amaranthaceae (read 2026-10-17): lamina simple and undivided, margins entire. Wikipedia Amaranthus (read 2026-10-17): leaves whole and simple. Wikipedia Atriplex: blade entire, toothed or lobed, so lobing occurs in that large genus.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 181: Ronse De Craene (Amaranthaceae incl. Chenopodiaceae): tepals mostly 3 to 5, rarely 1 or none; Simpson p. 371 gives 3-5 for Amaranthaceae s.s. and 5 (1, 6-8) for Chenopodiaceae. The rare 1-tepal flowers are left out because merosity starts at 2.

traits.stamens.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 181: stamens as many as the tepals and opposite them, rarely fewer; general formula 5, rarely 1 or up to 8-9.

traits.carpels.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 181, 182: ovary of 2 to 3 carpels, unilocular (general formula up to 6). Simpson p. 371 calls Amaranthaceae s.s. unicarpellous and Chenopodiaceae 2-3 (rarely 5).

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 371, 505: Simpson calls both Amaranthaceae s.s. and Chenopodiaceae hypogynous. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 283 Chenopodiaceae and 284 Amaranthaceae, which APG joins as Amaranthaceae: annual or perennial herbs, some undershrubs and shrubs (saltbushes, Salsola); leaves alternate, sometimes opposite, simple; no stipules; flowers small, regular, often green, in spikes, heads or racemes among dry bracts; a calyx of 3 to 5 lobes, often dry, and no petals, read here as one whorl of tepals; ovary superior, of one cell with one ovule; fruit a one-seeded nut that stays shut (read as an achene) or opens by a lid.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Amaranthaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Chenopodiaceae, Dysphaniaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded usually no rosette, rarely a basal rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 371, family Amaranthaceae: leaf margin entire, usually; read as {"entire": "usually"}.

traits.sexual_system.note: DELTA Amaranthaceae (read 2026-10-17) codes the plants as hermaphrodite (usually), with monoecy, dioecy and mixed states as less common; Wikipedia Amaranthaceae (read 2026-10-17, ~2,000-2,500 spp with the chenopods) also says most flowers are bisexual. Unisexual groups (Atriplex, Amaranthus, Iresine) are a minority. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.life_span.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 371, family Amaranthaceae: life span annual or perennial; read as {"annual": "often", "perennial": "often"}.

traits.fruit_type.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add berry (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 371: capsule (irregularly dehiscent) or berry.
